decisions.reason: As a medium-sized German machinery firm, we are likely to persist with a resin injection unit that had its own product page in both 2018 and 2019 because it reflects clear investment, public commitment, and close fit with our coating-equipment business.

Even if overlap with another resin injection unit raises some rationalization risk, the sunk development effort and visible market commitment make us more likely to continue than to withdraw it quickly.
The automatic airless spray gun appears central to the firm's application equipment range, so escalation of commitment and strategic fit both favor keeping it on the market.
The manual airless spray gun is somewhat more exposed to portfolio pruning, but as an established member of the launched spray-gun family it would still usually be retained for now.
Because the air-assisted airless spray gun broadens the firm's core spraying portfolio and was prominently presented after launch, management is likely to stay committed to it.
The data logger's reduced visibility from a standalone page in 2018 to only a mention in 2019 suggests weaker commitment and easier justification for withdrawal despite prior investment.
